questions.q: How does this lesson's "multi-instance" question differ from the Dev/Test/Prod pattern covered in DevOps, Testing & Deployment?
options: Dev/Test/Prod is about promoting one application through environments on the way to production; this lesson asks whether an organization needs more than one production instance itself
They are exactly the same question asked twice
Dev/Test/Prod only applies to scoped applications, never to this lesson's topic
This lesson replaces the need for Dev/Test/Prod entirely
questions.explain: Dev/Test/Prod is a delivery-pipeline question every org needs; a second production instance is a much rarer, separate architectural decision.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, legitimate reason an organization might run a second production instance?
options: A manager personally prefers a second instance for no stated business reason
A regulatory data-residency law requiring a defined category of data to physically stay within a specific region's infrastructure
The team wants to avoid learning Domain Separation
Two teams dislike sharing a single login page
questions.explain: A genuine data-residency requirement that a single instance's available regions can't satisfy is one of the two real justifications this lesson covers.

questions.q: What is ServiceNow's standard architectural guidance for multi-tenancy needs that could be satisfied within one instance?
options: Always provision a new production instance per department
Favor a single production instance and use Domain Separation for multi-tenancy needs within it, wherever real constraints allow
Multi-tenancy is never possible on ServiceNow
Avoid Domain Separation entirely and rely only on separate instances
questions.explain: The standard guidance defaults to one production instance with Domain Separation, reserving a second instance for constraints that genuinely can't be satisfied otherwise.

questions.q: What specific cost gets multiplied every single release cycle once an organization runs two production instances instead of one?
options: Nothing changes operationally between one and two instances
Only the initial setup cost, which is paid once
Upgrades, platform-wide security/ACL maintenance, integration endpoints, and monitoring/alerting all have to happen on two instances instead of one, indefinitely
The cost only applies to the first year after the second instance is created
questions.explain: Every ongoing platform-operations responsibility repeats once per production instance, for as long as both instances exist.

questions.q: Before recommending a second production instance, what should a Technical Architect confirm first?
options: That the requesting team has budget approval, with no further technical analysis needed
That the constraint (regulatory or business-independence) is real and genuinely cannot be satisfied by a single instance with Domain Separation and strong access controls
That a second instance is always cheaper than Domain Separation
Nothing — a second instance should be approved whenever any team requests one
questions.explain: The architect's job is to test whether the stated constraint is real and unsatisfiable within one instance before accepting the larger ongoing cost of a second one.
